claims.text: Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio liquid-state data can more accurately represent atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids than traditional EAM references.
Using MLP reference potentials will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in free-energy calculations.
MLPs can replace EAM reference potentials within the TOR-TILD thermodynamic-integration framework.
The proposed method applies at approximately 0.9–1.0 times the melting temperature.
The proposed method applies to alloys containing five or more principal elements typical of high-entropy systems.
An MLP trained directly on high-temperature ab initio molecular-dynamics liquid data captures many-body interactions.
Such an MLP captures the diversity of local atomic configurations in the high-temperature liquid.
Capturing many-body interactions and liquid structural fluctuations improves overlap between the reference and target phase spaces.
Improved phase-space overlap reduces mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path relative to EAM references.
MLP references are predicted to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately one order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Using MLP references will produce free-energy predictions closer to full ab initio results.
Conventional EAM references in TOR-TILD exhibit non-negligible integration-path mismatch.
The EAM integration-path mismatch arises from inadequate representation of the rich atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
The expected improvement is specific to multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting points.
MLP references may provide smaller benefits for elemental or binary systems because EAM potentials already give reasonable phase-space overlap in those systems.
A reduction of less than or equal to fivefold in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch would falsify the stated performance hypothesis.
